acceptance: Tests cover: regression over threshold exits 3; a slowdown under the threshold or under the minimum deltas exits 0; incomparable variants exit 4; incomparable timing modes exit 4 in both result-file mode and platform-run mode; a missing or corrupt result file exits 1; a usage error exits 2.
--allow-heterogeneous-comparison still bypasses the variant refusal, after which the normal codes apply.
compare --help and the user documentation list the codes, and the changelog.d fragment marks the change as breaking.
The perf step in .github/workflows/nightly-v2.yml still fails its job on a regression; the PR states how this was checked.
Smoke: run compare on real bundles for each of the four outcomes and show the exit status of each.
context:
Origin: adversarial review of an agent-facing strategy for BenchBox, 2026-11-12. Owner decisions quoted here were made on that date. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Evidence: the --fail-on-regression help text says 'Fail (exit 1)'; the two incomparable branches in the file-comparison path call sys.exit(1); the platform-run path raises ValueError wrapping IncomparableModesError.

Decision gate (before coding): search core workflows, the Makefile, scripts, tests and the benchbox-site docs for anything that matches compare's exit status exactly 1. List the consumers in the PR. If 3 or 4 already has a documented meaning anywhere in the CLI, stop and report; do not pick other numbers silently.

Verification rubric: pass only if each outcome has a test that would fail under the old single code, the four-outcome smoke is shown, and no other command's exit status changes.

Related, not duplicated: nightly-perf-gate-sensitivity-review-20261010 and perf-smoke-rebaseline-after-power-query-generation-20261103 own the nightly gate's thresholds and baseline.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items are delivered together on one feature branch and one PR, as their umbrella item names (site work: BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site); squash-merged. Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Review note (2026-11-13): this item's code table is the convention for later items. run-billable-platform-guard-noninteractive-20261113 needs a code for 'refused, acknowledgement required' and cli-results-integrity-validate-command-20261112 needs one for 'validation failed'. Document the table in one place so they can extend it without collision.

Revision (2026-11-13), after an independent critique and owner decisions: scripts/host_lock.py already uses exit codes 75 to 79; keep clear of them. The nightly perf step fails on any non-zero code, so it is unaffected.

Closeout (2026-11-13): delivered by https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4203, merged to develop as 5ba48a6796, with the external reviewer's SHIP and no open findings on head 862158097e. Checked on origin/develop: the billable-platform guard modules, the host_load block in benchbox/core/results/environment.py and the exit-code table are present. The delivering agent reported: compare exits 0/1/2/3/4 on a real bundle smoke; results validate exits 5 on FAIL and matches the MCP tool; the guard exits 6 before any credential read or connection, MCP accepts it only from the environment at server start, dry-run is exempt; host load is recorded at start and end, null for DataFrame adapters, which never took the snapshot. One required CI job failed once on an unrelated UAT timing test and passed on rerun. For the owner: the validator fails 89 of 491 published bundles, 74 of them ranking-eligible (mostly SF1 row counts and required keys; BigQuery and Snowflake 25 each); run --dry-run still reads credentials and may make network calls; platform credentials are stored in plaintext in ~/.benchbox/credentials.yaml; publish and submit ask no confirmation once a destination or token exists; run-official can acknowledge only via the environment variable; site documentation for the exit codes, validate command, guard and host-load fields is not yet written (text is in the PR body).
description:
Problem: benchbox compare exits 1 when a regression exceeds --fail-on-regression, when two results are not comparable (IncomparableVariantsError, IncomparableModesError), and on ordinary errors. A pipeline cannot tell 'slower' from 'cannot compare' from 'broken'.

Owner decision (2026-11-12): distinct codes now; the breaking change is accepted because the project is pre-1.0. Codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error (Click default, unchanged), 3 regression over threshold, 4 not comparable.

Non-goals: exit codes of run and every other command; thresholds, minimum-delta semantics and comparison maths; JSON output shape.
